title: 'Shoot me, shoot me': Inquiry begins into case of man killed by Edmonton police officer
subtitle: The police officer who shot a man twice during a confrontation in a west Edmonton alley more than four years ago said Monday he believed he was about to be attacked. Kinling Robin Fire, 39, died March 31, 2011, after he was shot in the chest by Const. Brendan Power in an alley near 156th Street and 100th Avenue.
article: EDMONTON - The police officer who shot a man twice during a confrontation in a west Edmonton alley more than four years ago said Monday he believed he was about to be attacked.
Kinling Robin Fire, 39, died March 31, 2011, after he was shot in the chest by Const. Brendan Power in an alley near 156th Street and 100th Avenue.
"There was no doubt in my mind he was going to attack me," Power testified Monday at a fatality inquiry.
Fire's sister, Wanda Bearboy, spoke on behalf of Fire's family during the proceedings.
"When you did shoot him, how come you shot him twice?" she asked Power.
Power said he remembered Fire was still coming toward him after he fired the first shot.
In 2012, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team found Power's actions were justified.
The incident started late on March 30 when Power and Const. Brent Fox were investigating the report of a man, later identified as Fire, who was suicidal.
Another call came in about a possibly impaired driver, with a vehicle description that matched a vehicle belonging to Fire.
The officers located Fire and followed the vehicle into an icy alley. Fire did not exit the vehicle and Power used his baton to smash the driver's window.
"When I looked at him, he's looking at me absolutely enraged," Power said.
Fire then began moving toward Power holding a metal bar, Power said.
Meanwhile, Fox was in the patrol car and tried "nudging" Fire using the car. Neither officer had a Taser.
Fox testified he wanted to get Fire's attention. Fire did fall down, but got back up with the object still in his hand, the officers said.
Power said Fire charged at him, saying "Shoot me, shoot me."
Insp. Alan Murphy, a sergeant at the time of the incident, arrived as the events were unfolding. He was concerned Power would get hurt, he said Monday.
Power fired two shots and Fire fell to his knees. Fire struggled with the officers as they tried to handcuff him.
Next, Power said he unwrapped a bandage and applied pressure to Fire's chest.
Const. Lisa Dack testified she arrived at the scene minutes after the shots were fired and had to cut off Fire's clothes to put bandages on his wounds. She did not see Power, she said.
Dack rode in an ambulance with Fire and paramedics. When Fire was asked if he had any allergies, he said he was allergic to cops, Dack said.
Fire died around 4 a.m. in hospital. He had a high concentration of sleeping pills in his system when he died.
The inquiry is scheduled for two days, after which provincial court Judge Steven Bilodeau will compile a report and may make recommendations.
